title: Anti-aliased editor grid floor material
purpose: Draw an editor ground grid in three.js: minor and major lines of a fixed pixel width anti-aliased from screen-space derivatives, red and blue axis lines, moire suppression and a distance fade, with exact CPU mirrors of the coverage. Use it for level editors, model viewers and debug views.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE under WebGL 2 (fwidth and the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createGridFloorMaterial
exports.summary: The transparent, double-sided grid for a horizontal plane; an unknown option throws TypeError.

exports.name: gridLineCoverage
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the coverage of the nearest grid line, with the moire fade.

exports.name: gridAxisCoverage
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the coverage of the axis line through 0.

exports.name: gridFade
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the distance fade.

exports.name: GRID_FLOOR_FRAGMENT
exports.summary: Fragment stage: lines from fwidth of world x and z, axis colours and fade.

options.name: xAxisColor
options.meaning: Colour of the line along X (z = 0).

options.name: zAxisColor
options.meaning: Colour of the line along Z (x = 0).

options.name: fadeStart
options.meaning: Camera distance where the fade starts.

options.name: fadeEnd
options.meaning: Camera distance where the grid is gone.

limits: A flat plane in world x and z: the grid does not follow a curved or tilted mesh, and because it writes no depth it never hides objects below it; place it at the height you want. Line widths come from per-pixel derivatives of world coordinates, so at grazing angles lines blur and the moire fade removes dense lines early. There is no level-of-detail switch to coarser spacings as the camera rises, only the fade. Transparent sorting follows three.js object order. Written for three.js r155 or later; only 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Screen-space line width from fwidth of world coordinates
Distance to the nearest grid line with fract
Smoothstep distance fade from the camera
